how: Read from evidence/STRATEGY_IDEAS_INPUT.json, which tools/strategy_ideas.py extracted from each canonical file (docstring, settings, indicator calls, entry/exit conditions, method inventory), plus a direct read of the files whose conditions are built in helper variables, plus user_data/family_deltas.py for the version-to-version notes: it compares consecutive revisions of a family and prints settings changes, added and removed indicator calls and methods, the changed conditions and the size. Every sentence names the code fact it rests on in `evidence`. Each family names the one revision it was read from in `read_from`, with that revision's source_sha256; tools/strategy_ideas.py --check compares it against the corpus and the page marks it stale when the corpus has moved on. The family's other rows are derived from the corpus by stem, so nothing here lists 39 hashes to say what the corpus already knows.
scope: nineteen families in two batches: ten that the published family table leads with (Zaratustra, Slope, RSIBB, EMA + Fibonacci, el_extrema, Rsiqui, BollingerMACD, GnF, EWOist, PlusMinus) and the ten largest stems in the corpus (E0V1E, Zaratustra, Ichimoku, CombinedBinHAndCluc, BinH, NostalgiaForInfinityX, NostalgiaForInfinityNext, roger, GeneTrader_gen, VWAPStrategy). Zaratustra is in both batches. The corpus holds about 2,000 stems; everything here is a sample.

families.idea: One comparison decides everything: while RSI(7) sits above RSI(14) the strategy is long, while it sits below it is short, and each side is closed as soon as the two cross back. There is no other filter and no signal-per-candle logic - the position is a state of the RSI spread. Exits in practice come from the risk settings, which are deliberately tight: 1% stoploss, 0.1% trailing stop and a flat 1% take-profit.
families.caveat: The site's own family table advertises this family as 10x with a trailing stop. This revision's leverage() returns 1, so the published description and the code in the corpus disagree about position size - the description there may belong to a different revision or to a bot configuration.

populate_exit_trend: exit_long where rsi7 < rsi14, exit_short where rsi7 > rsi14
settings: minimal_roi {'0': 0.01}, stoploss -0.01, trailing_stop True, trailing_stop_positive 0.001

families.idea: Perfect trend alignment on Fibonacci-length EMAs: EMA(34/55/89/144/233) of the typical price, and the long requires the +DI series of the same lengths stacked in ascending order (34>55>89>144>233) with the last one above -DI; the short mirrors it on the -DI side. The exit throws the trade out on any cross of the price with the 233 EMA, so the strategy rides an aligned trend but leaves as soon as price loses the longest average. The 0.99 stoploss is nominal - the exit signal is the real risk control.

families.idea: Dip-buying at detected extrema with an EWO momentum filter: a local minimum of the close (argrelextrema, order 5) plus price below EMA(entry length) times low_offset, and then either an EWO above the high threshold with RSI below the entry level or an EWO below the low threshold, opens the long; the short side is the mirror at local maxima. Exits are the ROI ladder (50% at entry decaying to 2% after five days) plus a 5% stoploss. The offsets, EMA lengths, RSI level and both EWO thresholds are hyperopt parameters, so the revision in the corpus is one point in a search space.

families.idea: The trigger is the slope of an EMA-smoothed RSI, not the RSI level alone: long when RSI is below the entry level and the smoothed RSI gradient turns up, short when RSI is above the upper level and the gradient turns down; each side closes when the gradient turns against it and RSI has crossed the exit level. It is a mean-reversion scalp at 5m with hyperopt-driven thresholds (entry 30-70) and a steep ROI ladder (22% decaying to 0 after ~110 minutes) over a 27% stoploss.

families.idea: A synthetic greed/fear index decides the direction: momentum (close against SMA20), volatility (NATR14) and a volume sentiment (up-volume minus down-volume) are each min-max normalised over a 20-bar window and averaged into one 0-1 number. Above 0.7 the strategy is long, below 0.3 short, and a trade is only opened while volume exceeds its own 50-bar mean; the opposite threshold closes the side, so the index crossing the band is what turns the position.

families.idea: A directional-indicator breakout with an RSI filter: +DI crossing above -DI while RSI is above 60 opens the long, -DI crossing above +DI while RSI is below 15 opens the short, and the same crosses close the opposite side. families.idea: A 5m scalper whose entry is a bundle of conditions ORed together rather than one rule: EMA(8/16) against EMA/SMA(15) and RSI(4/14/20), the stochastic-fast fastk, and a Bollinger band around the typical price are collected into a list and reduced with `lambda x, y: x | y`, so any single member can open a trade. The exit side is where the work sits: a custom_stoploss that locks in above 1% profit and treats trades tagged 'ewo' differently, plus a custom_exit that reads the fastk and RSI columns of the current candle. minimal_roi and the 0.99 stoploss are nominal next to that.
families.caveat: The custom_stoploss branches on the entry tag (`if 'ewo' in enter_tags`), so the same file holds two different exit rules depending on which condition opened the trade - a reader who evaluates only the stoploss number will read the risk wrong.

versions.note: The only chronology this family has, and it comes from the dates in five file names: the ROI goes {'0': 10} -> {'0': 0.02, '120': 0.01} -> {'0': 10} -> {'0': 1} -> {'0': 10}, the stoploss -0.13 -> -0.18 -> -0.27 -> back to -0.99, startup_candle_count 121 -> 120 -> 20, and the 2024-01-11 revision adds ta.CCI(20) and switches DCA (position_adjustment_enable) off again. Five dated rows, four steps, and they are steps of a scalar search rather than four designs.

families.idea: The Ichimoku cloud used as a filter around a Tenkan/Kijun cross rather than as the signal itself: the long needs the Tenkan line to cross above the Kijun line while the cloud is red, and the short is not the mirror but a different rule. Later revisions keep the same cross and read the cloud from a higher timeframe through informative_pairs, or replace the candle with its Heikin-Ashi version and compare that against the daily Senkou A/B - so the family is one idea read against different chart types.
families.caveat: The entry in the row read here buys a Tenkan/Kijun cross while `cloud_red` is true, i.e. while the cloud is bearish - the opposite of the textbook reading, where a cross is only taken in the direction of the cloud. Its `populate_sell_trend` also assigns an empty tuple, so exits in this revision come from minimal_roi alone.

families.idea: The X line is a trading system rather than a signal: an entry built from a long list of indexed conditions, a custom_exit of several hundred lines, adjust_trade_position for DCA and a set of _bad_trade_controller_* handlers that decide when a losing trade gets de-risked, held or closed. families.idea: The numbered rows are one line of work: each iteration adds a candlestick-pattern filter to a VWAP/EMA/RSI/ATR frame, until roger27 trades `bullish_conditions | candlestick_patterns & macd_condition` and stops the trade on peak-profit drawdown. families.caveat: `roger` (88 lines, nine conditions) and `VWAPStrategy` (73 lines) use the same construction: a per-candle state column asking whether the body touched the daily VWAP from below, above or both, plus RSI percentile bands. They are not code-identical, which is why no duplicate verdict covers them, but a reader should expect them to behave alike.

read_from.note: the undecorated row, 73 lines, the smallest of the 18

families.idea: A VWAP band system: for every candle the code asks whether the body touched the daily VWAP from below, from above or both, stores that as a state column, and then asks the RSI(16) to sit below its own 10th percentile (or the mirror, above the 90th) while the close is outside the Bollinger band - so the trade needs a VWAP event, an RSI extreme and a band break at once, joined with reduce(lambda x, y: x & y, conditions). The stop is a custom_stoploss that is rewritten in almost every row of the family; the entry is not.
families.caveat: The rows here are numbered by the harvest, and the numbers do not order them: VWAPStrategy_11 has stoploss -0.1, _12 has -0.2 and drops the trailing stop, and the undecorated row has -0.07 again. The table below lists variants, not a history.

versions.label: the entry
versions.note: Unchanged across all 18 rows: the VWAP_signal loop, RSI(16) with percentile bands, Bollinger(14, 2). This is one of the few families where the signal and the risk can be separated cleanly.

versions.label: the stop block
versions.note: custom_stoploss is rewritten in nearly every row - 35 -> 31 -> 28 -> 27 -> 25 -> 28 -> 18 -> 17 -> 21 lines - and changes its idea twice: it starts from the ATR, then compares the current profit against fixed steps, then works from trade.initial_stop_loss, and VWAPStrategy_1 arms it with ta.atr(length=150) where the undecorated row uses length=7.

versions.label: the variants
versions.note: use_custom_stoploss is absent at _2 and present from _03 on; the stoploss moves between -0.2 and -0.1 twice; trailing_stop, trailing_stop_positive and the offset appear and disappear together (at _12 and again at _18). None of the moves is reversed later in a way that would let one call this a direction.
